styles.city: A page from an explorer's field sketchbook, drawn on the spot, in the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries (Cook's artists, Conrad Martens on the Beagle, Thomas Baines with Livingstone, Edward Wilson in the Antarctic). A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink over parts of it, with loose parallel hatching for shade; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue, pooling and leaving the paper bare in places. The drawing is unfinished: detail is concentrated on the city, and the edges, the sky and the near water dissolve into bare cream paper in an irregular vignette. Slightly foxed, worn sketchbook paper with soft tone variation; a single page, no binding or spine visible. An observed working sketch, not a finished painting. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, dates or signature. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given.
styles.journey: An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found, rather than a distant landscape. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.
